title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The 'loop equations' are the 2-cycle and 3-cycle type relations later familiar from Drinfeld's GT. Here they are studied through GL(2,Ẑ) acting on the congruence closure of Π_0, a lift of Γ(2) to SL(2,Z), so essentially π_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. On the previous page, solutions are sought as triples x(u) = (τ(u), τ'(a), τ(b)) ≡ (u, εa, εb). The essential congruence is (94): uτ(u)^{-1} ≡ ε a τ'(a)^{-1} mod Π̂_0.

Why u is not in GL(2,Z). Elements of GL(2,Z) satisfy ε_2ε_3 = 1, but the u sought needs ε_2(u)ε_3(u) = -1. So Grothendieck works in GL(2,Ẑ) and takes u = diag(μ,1) with μ ≡ -1 (3), μ ≡ 1 (4), i.e. μ ≡ 5 (12).

This page.
(i) With τ = diag(-1,1), u and τ commute, so uτ(u)^{-1} = 1. Condition (94) therefore reduces to a τ'(a)^{-1} ≡ ε mod Π̂_0.
(ii) Ansatz (96): a = τ' a_0 with a_0 = cρ + d.
- Here ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] has order 6, and a_0 lies in Ẑ[ρ] ≅ Ẑ[ω], i.e. Eisenstein integers realised as the centraliser of the order-6 elliptic element.
- Its determinant is the norm N(a_0) = c²+cd+d², which must be a unit.
- τ' = [[0,1],[1,0]].
- Then (97): a = [[-c, c+d],[d, c]], and (98): μ = det a = -(c²+cd+d²).
- Since a unit Eisenstein norm is ≡ 1 mod 3, automatically μ ≡ -1 (3), which matches ε_3. The condition μ ≡ 1 (4) forces c ≡ 2 (4) and d odd.
(iii) The group Π_0 ⊂ SL(2,Z) is generated by -l_0, -l_1, -l_∞, with l_0 = [[1,-2],[0,1]], l_1 = [[1,0],[2,1]], l_∞ = [[3,-2],[2,-1]].
- One checks (-l_1)(-l_0)(-l_∞) = 1.
- Π_0 is a complement of ±1 in Γ(2), free of rank 2 and of index 12. It contains Γ(4), so it is a congruence subgroup and SL(2,Ẑ)/Π̂_0 ≅ SL(2,Z)/Π_0.
- This quotient is presented as the dicyclic (binary dihedral) group of order 12: ρ⁶ = σ⁴ = 1, ρ³ = σ², σρσ^{-1} = ρ^{-1}.
(iv) GL(2,Ẑ)/Π̂_0 is an extension of Ẑ^* (via det) by this group. It splits as a semidirect product via the torus T_0 = {diag(ξ,1)} ≅ Ẑ^*, which acts on Dic_3 through ε_2 (ξ mod 4) [references to pp. 593', 599, formulas (33), (35), (35bis)].
(v) The method is to find σ with (99): σa ≡ u mod Π̂_0, where σ = [[0,-1],[1,0]].
- (100): σa = [[-d,-c],[-c,c+d]], which is correct.
- On the next page this is turned into the parity conditions c ≡ 0, d ≡ 1 (2) and a Lemma: a τ'(a)^{-1} ≡ ε mod Π̂_0 with ε independent of c, d.

Purpose. To produce explicit 'non-GL(2,Z)' solutions of the loop equations, of determinant μ ≡ 5 mod 12, built from the norm-one-type torus of the Eisenstein order, and to determine the sign ε.
errors: No computational errors on this page. Checked: (cρ+d) = [[d,c],[-c,c+d]]; τ'(cρ+d) = [[-c,c+d],[d,c]]; det = -(c²+cd+d²); σa = [[-d,-c],[-c,c+d]].
The generators -l_0, -l_1, -l_∞ satisfy (-l_1)(-l_0)(-l_∞) = 1. This product relation is only in that order, as written; the order is not stated on the page.
The equation number written as (95) on this page is almost certainly (96): (95) was already used on the previous page, and the next one here is (97).
On the next page the Lemma says 'c, d ∈ Ẑ^*', which contradicts c ≡ 0 (2). It should read c, d ∈ Ẑ.

ideas.what: Using elements of the Eisenstein Cartan torus Ẑ[ρ]^* (centraliser of the order-6 elliptic element), twisted by τ', to manufacture GL(2,Ẑ) elements whose determinant is -N(a_0), forced ≡ -1 mod 3
ideas.modern_name: non-split Cartan subgroup at the CM point j=0; norms from Z[ω]

ideas.what: Π_0 = torsion-free lift of Γ(2) generated by -l_0, -l_1, -l_∞, with SL(2,Z)/Π_0 ≅ dicyclic group of order 12, and GL(2,Ẑ)/Π̂_0 ≅ Dic_3 ⋊ Ẑ^* with Ẑ^* acting through ε_2
ideas.modern_name: congruence quotient of the Legendre-family monodromy group; π_1 of P^1-{0,1,∞} inside SL(2,Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; used in GT literature (Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (circulated 1981) treats SL(2,Z) and Γ(2) material; exact content unsure

ideas.what: Seeking solutions of the loop (2-cycle/3-cycle) equations in GL(2,Ẑ) with ε_2ε_3 = -1, i.e. not coming from GL(2,Z), with determinant ≡ 5 mod 12, and determining an intrinsic sign ε
ideas.modern_name: elements of a GT-type group (GT_0 / genus-one GT) realised through the congruence quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps for GT and its genus-one variants

missed.claim: Grothendieck builds explicit GL(2,Ẑ) candidates for 'exotic' solutions of the loop equations (ε_2ε_3 = -1) from Eisenstein norm data, aiming at an intrinsic sign ε, i.e. a character on such solutions. The fate of this sign and its relation to the GT characters is not settled on this page.
missed.quote: a = τ' a_0, a_0 = cρ + d, c²+cd+d² ∈ Ẑ^* ... μ = -(c²+cd+d²) ... σ a ≡ u (Π̂_0)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor explicit check on whether the congruence image of GT-type solutions carries a sign obstruction. It is probably subsumed by known descriptions of the image of GT in GL(2,Ẑ)/congruence quotients, but it is a concrete unpublished computation.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but routine matrix computation within a larger unpublished exploration of the loop equations. The Eisenstein-torus device and the Dic_3 ⋊ Ẑ^* quotient are standard. It is mildly interesting as evidence of Grothendieck testing non-GL(2,Z) congruence solutions, but nothing here seems to be a new result.
transcription_corrections: Top page number: likely '606' in the image, not '506', consistent with the references to pp. 593', 599.
'u τ(u) s^{-1} = 1' should read 'u τ(u)^{-1} = 1': u and τ are both diagonal and commute.
Equation label '(95)' on this page is likely '(96)'.
'On travaillera avec le groupe formé' is more plausibly 'On travaillera avec le groupe Π_0 dans SL(2,Z) engendré par'.
The line after the presentation reads roughly 'et ce produit devient semi-direct grâce à' T_0. The marginal insertion is 'par l'intermédiaire de ε_2(ξ)' ('opérant par l'intermédiaire de ε_2').
Before (99), read roughly 'On écrira (déf)' rather than 'On [?] déf'.
Margin note: 'un peu bref… cf plus bas'.
